chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Hamza ibn Humran, who said:

A man complained to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and said: 'The Jinn have driven us out of our homes.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Make the ceilings of your houses seven cubits high, and place the bathroom in the fringes of the house.' The man said: 'So we did that, and we did not see anything we disliked after that.'
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended architectural remedy for Jinn disturbance in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) prescribes specific architectural modifications—raising ceilings to seven cubits and situating bathrooms (*kanaf al-dar*) away from living quarters—as a practical remedy for Jinn disturbance. This reflects the Shia scholarly understanding of the physical environment's role in spiritual well-being, linking domestic hygiene and spatial design to the mitigation of unseen forces. The companion’s testimony confirms the efficacy of this prophetic tradition in daily life, emphasizing the integration of faith with practical domestic arrangements.
